claim_tested: For the repository-effect-admission-single-cas-v1 route, a lost acknowledgement can be classified on a later scheduled-Chat invocation using only the designated canonical-head file plus immutable predecessor-linked record data: (a) candidate is current committed tip, (b) candidate committed and remains a canonical ancestor after later authorized head-file advances, or (c) candidate never became canonical. classification.a_current_tip: Read the canonical-head file. If its committed tip identity equals the candidate identity, the candidate is the current canonical committed tip.
classification.b_committed_ancestor: If the current tip is later, follow exact predecessor identities through immutable retained records. Finding the candidate before genesis classifies it as a committed canonical ancestor after later authorized advancement.
classification.c_never_canonical: If traversal reaches the canonical genesis/root without the candidate, then under the tested protocol invariants the candidate never became canonical, even if a PREPARED record file exists.

verification_result.why_lost_ack_is_recoverable: Acceptance is defined by canonical-chain membership rather than by receipt of the write acknowledgement. A later invocation can re-read the canonical head and deterministic predecessor chain, so acknowledgement loss does not erase the committed-state evidence.
verification_result.material_scope_correction: GitHub's Contents API does not itself enforce the logical predecessor-chain invariant, append-only record immutability, monotonic generation/sequence discipline, or absence of out-of-protocol rewrites. Therefore the three-way classification is source-supported only for protocol-conformant authorized writers and retained immutable records. Bare endpoint semantics alone are insufficient to prove those higher-level invariants.
verification_result.aba_note: The update guard is the target file's blob SHA, i.e. content identity. If an out-of-protocol writer can restore byte-identical prior canonical-head content, a stale writer could encounter the same blob SHA again. The tested route therefore still requires monotonic/non-repeating head content and protocol-conformant writers; exact ABA resistance is left as the next unresolved leaf.

hard_gate_assessment.rate_limit_behavior: per-window limitation; recover by cross-invocation checkpoint/resume, never in-run waiting
